title: Route collision risk between dynamic and static routes
reasoning: The routing configuration has catch-all dynamic routes (/:clientSlug and /:clientSlug/chat) defined after specific static routes. While React Router v6 prioritizes more specific routes, there's a risk of collision if any value in PORTAL_CONFIGS.slug matches existing static routes (like 'status', 'mro', 'rag-demo', etc.). The order and precedence is unclear without seeing PORTAL_CONFIGS content, and route definition order matters for catch-alls.
reproduction: If PORTAL_CONFIGS contains a slug like 'status' or 'mro', navigating to /status might incorrectly render Portal instead of StatusPage, depending on route matching order.
recommendation: 1) Audit PORTAL_CONFIGS to ensure no slugs collide with static routes. 2) Add runtime validation that throws an error if a config slug matches a reserved route. 3) Consider namespacing dynamic portals under a prefix like /portal/:clientSlug to avoid collisions. 4) Add explicit route tests.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for this feature. Route matching logic and collision detection are not tested.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that: 1) Verify all static routes resolve correctly, 2) Test that PORTAL_CONFIGS slugs don't overlap with reserved routes, 3) Validate dynamic routes only match when no static route exists.
minimumFixScope: src/src/main.tsx routing logic + add validation in PORTAL_CONFIGS definition
